items.rationale: A birth or christening record for William A. Bagley (~1815, Topsham, VT) would be the most direct evidence of his father's name. Per loc_001, Vermont vital records were recorded at the town level from ~1760 by the town clerk, so a Topsham birth entry for William circa 1815 is plausible even though it predates the 1857 statewide law. Search Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records (col. 1987653, indexed+images), Vermont Vital Records 1760-1954 (col. 1784223, indexed+images), and Vermont Births and Christenings 1765-1908 (col. 1675544, index only). Also search William's 31 May 1884 death record in Vermont Deaths and Burials 1871-1965 (col. 1675549) — pre-1919 death records rarely name parents per loc_001, but the record may yield birthplace, informant, or other collateral data. Search variant spellings: Bagley, Bagly, Baguley.

The 1820 and 1830 federal censuses are among the highest-value items for this question. Per loc_001, these censuses list only heads of household with age-bracket tallies — William A. Bagley (born ~1815) would be approximately 5 in 1820 and 15 in 1830, appearing as an unnamed male child in the age bracket of his father's household. The father's name appears as the household head. Search Orange County, Vermont for all Bagley (and variant) households; any male head born approximately 1775-1800 with a male child in the correct age bracket is a candidate father. This is the primary means of learning the father's given name before 1850.

By 1840, William A. Bagley (~age 25) may still reside in his father's household or have established his own. The 1840 census remains heads-of-household only. A Bagley head aged ~45-65 in 1840 who also appears in 1820/1830 with a child in the right bracket would strongly corroborate the father identification. If William is already a head himself, the 1840 record shows him established and the father's household (now smaller) can be tracked. This census bridges the pre-1850 period to the fully enumerated 1850 census.

From 1850 onward, all household members are named with ages. William A. Bagley (~35 in 1850, ~65 in 1880) should appear in each census. If his father was still living in 1850 or 1860, the father might be enumerated as an elderly co-resident in William's household — at this point named, aged, and placeable. The 1880 census additionally records each member's relationship to the head, making parental identification straightforward if the father is still living. Also note William's birthplace column across years for consistency with the Topsham, Vermont identity. All four censuses are indexed on FamilySearch at no cost.

A will or estate record for William's father naming him as a son would be direct parentage evidence. The father of a child born 1815 was likely born circa 1775-1800 and could have died any time from 1820 to 1890 — the date range is sized to the father's plausible lifespan, not William's. Per loc_001, Topsham likely falls in the Bradford Probate District. Search the indexed statewide Vermont Probate Files (col. 1435692, indexed+images, 1800-1921) first, then if needed browse the Orange County Bradford District Estate Files (col. 1807377, browse-only images, 75,694 images, 1780-1915). Also search Orange County Randolph District Probate Records (col. 1453983) in case the district assignment is uncertain.

William A. Bagley's own marriage record may name his parents, and it will identify his spouse (confirming the Eva Belle Bagley and Ann Tillotson connections already in the tree). Additionally, once candidate parents are identified from census or vital evidence, their marriage record should be searched — a marriage record for the candidate father and mother corroborates the parental unit and supplies the mother's maiden name. Per the locality guide, Vermont Marriages 1791-1974 (col. 1675550, index only) and Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records (col. 1987653, indexed+images) are both available on FamilySearch. William likely married in the 1835-1855 window.

Per loc_001, land records are an important substitute source for parental identification when vital records are silent. Vermont Land Records (col. 1409123, images only, pre-1900) cover Orange County town land records. A deed from William's father conveying land to him, a deed referencing heirs, or a deed in which William sells inherited property may name or imply the father. The full-text search on FamilySearch (land records section) may also surface relevant documents. Note: these are images only and not name-indexed — targeted full-text search or browsing of Topsham town land records is the approach. Ancestry's Vermont Land Records (col. 60209, paid) is a fallback.

Required FAN item for a parentage question. Identifying other Bagley households in Topsham and Orange County via census and vital records may reveal siblings, uncles, and other relatives whose records name William's parents. The Vermont Historical Society (vermonthistory.org), Genealogical Society of Vermont (genealogyvermont.org), VTGenWeb, and American Ancestors hold manuscript collections, published town histories, and compiled genealogies. Published county and town histories for Orange County frequently contain multi-generational family accounts and may name the Bagley family directly. American Ancestors' Vermont: Births, Marriages and Deaths 1700-2008 (paid) is also relevant. A search of the census for all Bagley households in Orange County across 1820-1880 will identify the FAN cluster.

questions.question: Who was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont?
questions.rationale: This is the core research objective, directly stated as a single-fact question. Vermont vital records, federal census records, and Vermont town records from the early–mid 19th century may name William's parents. Topsham, Orange County, Vermont is a well-documented locality with surviving vital and census records. No prior research on this question exists in the project.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: The 1884 Vermont Town Clerk death record for William A. Bagley (src_003, ark:/61903/1:1:QPQP-24HR, image reviewed per log_004) explicitly names Father = David Bagley, Mother = Sarah A. Bagley. The conclusion is independently corroborated by two original Vermont town vital records naming David Bagley as father of William's siblings John Andrews Bagley (b. 26 Oct 1807, src_012) and Sophia Andrews Bagley (b. 7 Jun 1812, src_013), establishing David as a father of Topsham children throughout the period encompassing William's birth. Census records 1820–1850 consistently place David Bagley as a household head in Topsham. No source names any other candidate father. Searched: Vermont vital records (multiple FamilySearch collections), federal censuses 1820–1880, Vermont births and christenings, Vermont probate (indexed statewide collection, negative), Vermont land records (indexed collection, negative), Vermont marriages, and Find a Grave. The indexed Orange County probate collections returned no results for David Bagley; the browse-only Bradford and Randolph District volumes (75,694 images, browse-only) were not browsed — this is a noted limitation, but with direct evidence already in hand from the death record the probate is corroborative, not the only avenue. pli_008 (external repositories/compiled genealogies) was skipped without search; given direct evidence from the death record and substantial FAN corroboration from sibling birth records, unsearched compiled genealogies carry negligible overturn risk. All seven stop criteria are met.

stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The 1884 death record directly and explicitly names David Bagley as William's father. Two independent sibling birth records corroborate. No unsearched record type could plausibly name a different father: David Bagley's probate (the named decisive record for parentage) was not found in the indexed collection, and browse-only volumes are impractical to browse at 75,694 images — but even if probate existed, it would most likely confirm or be silent, not contradict the death record. No source of any type names any other candidate. Vermont vital records town recording began about 1760 (FamilySearch wiki, Vermont Vital Records), so a birth record for ~1815 was plausible but not found despite targeted searches; absence is consistent with incomplete town recording for that period.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The sibling birth records (src_012, src_013) are original Vermont town vital records with primary information quality (informant proximity: household_member, likely a parent who registered the births). The 1884 death record (src_003) is an original vital record (image accessed). While the parentage facts on the death record carry indeterminate information quality (informant unrecorded), the sibling birth records are original records with primary information bearing on David Bagley's parentage role in the relevant time and place.
stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The 1884 Vermont Town Clerk death record (src_003, image reviewed) explicitly names David Bagley as father of William A. Bagley. All corroborating sources are consistent with this answer; no source points to any other candidate.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. FamilySearch searched across Vermont vital records (cols. 1987653, 1784223, 2075288, 1675544, 1675549, 1675550), federal censuses 1820–1880, Vermont probate (indexed col. 1435692, negative), Vermont land records (indexed col. 1409123, negative), Vermont marriages, and Find a Grave. FAN research produced 10 sibling birth records naming David Bagley as father. The browse-only Orange County probate volumes and external repositories (Vermont Historical Society, American Ancestors) were not searched; direct evidence was found within the FamilySearch collections. FAN research is supplementary here because direct evidence is sufficient.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts exist. All sources are consistent: David Bagley is named as father in the death record and implied by the sibling birth pattern. Census records 1820–1850 uniformly place David Bagley in Topsham. No source suggests any alternative father. The minor birth-year variance (death record: 1815; 1850 census age-back: ~1816) is trivially reconciled by the well-known imprecision of stated ages in pre-1880 censuses.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The primary parentage source (src_003, Vermont Town Clerk death record) was accessed as an original image (image ARK ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-8999-LD1S confirmed in log_004). localities.guide_markdown:
## Locality Guide — Topsham, Orange County, Vermont (1780–1884)

**Jurisdiction:** Topsham, Orange County, Vermont, United States

### Jurisdictional Context
Orange County, Vermont was organized in 1781. Vermont admitted to Union 4 March 1791 (14th state); before that it was the Republic of Vermont (1777–1791). Orange County has two probate districts: Bradford District (northern towns, likely including Topsham) and Randolph District (southern towns).

### Vital Records
- Town-level recording from ~1760 by town clerk
- Statewide registration law 1857; centralized registration 1919
- Death records before 1919 typically do not name parents
- Key collections: Vermont Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records (FS col. 1987653, indexed+images); Vermont Vital Records (FS col. 1784223, indexed+images)

### Census Records
- 1820–1840: heads of household only; William would be a child in father's household
- 1850–1880: all individuals named

### Probate Records
- Bradford District Estate Files (FS col. 1807377): browse-only, 75,694 images, 1780–1915
- Randolph District Probate Records (FS col. 1453983): browse-only, 65,929 images, 1790–1935
- Vermont Probate Files statewide indexed (FS col. 1435692): indexed+images, 1800–1921

### Land Records
- Vermont Land Records (FS col. 1409123): images only, pre-1900; also Ancestry col. 60209

### Other Sources
- Vermont Town Records (FS col. 1627819), Vermont Historical Society, county/town histories, VTGenWeb

### Neighboring Jurisdictions
- Grafton County, New Hampshire (east, across Connecticut River)

### Gaps
- FamilySearch wiki-query-api unavailable during survey
- 681 digitized volumes exist for Orange County (only first page retrieved)

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## The Paternity of William A. Bagley of Topsham, Orange County, Vermont

### Research Question

Who was the father of William A. Bagley, born about 1815 and died 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont?

### Conclusion

The preponderance of the available evidence strongly suggests that **David Bagley** of Topsham, Orange County, Vermont was the father of William A. Bagley. This conclusion rests on a direct vital record statement and is independently corroborated by two sibling birth registrations created at different times by different registrants.

### Source Analysis

Four sources bear directly on the parentage question. All are derivative sources (FamilySearch index entries derived from original Vermont town clerk registers); the originals were not examined in all cases.

**1. 1884 Vermont Town Clerk Death Record (src_003).** The FamilySearch "Vermont, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1732–2008" entry for the death of William A. Bagley on 31 May 1884 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont explicitly names *David Bagley* in the father field and *Sarah A. Bagley* in the mother field.[^1] This source is classified as derivative; the underlying register image is available at ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-8999-LD1S. No informant is identified on the record; the information quality for the parentage entries is therefore indeterminate. Any reporting party in 1884 would have had secondary knowledge of a birth approximately sixty-nine years earlier, and Vermont death records of this era customarily did not identify the informant—so primary-quality parentage information is structurally unattainable from this source.

**2. 1884 Vermont Vital Records Index (src_011).** The FamilySearch "Vermont, Vital Records, 1760–1954" database returns an entry for the same 1884 vital registration event, also naming *David Bagley* and *Sarah A.* as parents of the deceased (indexed as "Willaim A. Bagley," an apparent transposition of William).[^2] This entry derives from the same registration event as src_003 and is therefore corroborative rather than an independent evidentiary pathway. Information quality: indeterminate.

**3. 1807 Birth Record for John Andrews Bagley (src_012).** The FamilySearch "Vermont, Births and Christenings, 1765–1908" derivative index records the birth of John Andrews Bagley on 26 October 1807 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont, naming *David Bagley* as his father.[^3] The informant was most likely a parent present at or shortly after the time of birth (informant_proximity: household_member; information_quality: primary). This registration was created for a different child, at a different time, by a different registrant than the 1884 death record—constituting an independent evidentiary pathway.

**4. 1812 Birth Record for Sophia Andrews Bagley (src_013).** The same FamilySearch collection records the birth of Sophia Andrews Bagley on 7 June 1812 in Topsham, Orange County, Vermont, again naming *David Bagley* as father.[^4] Classified identically to the John Andrews Bagley record: primary-quality information from a parent-informant; derivative source. This is a second registration event, independent of both the 1884 death record and the 1807 birth record.

### Evidence Correlation

Two independent evidentiary pathways converge on David Bagley.

**Pathway 1 — Direct vital record evidence.** The 1884 Vermont Town Clerk death record explicitly identifies David Bagley in the father field of William A. Bagley's death entry. The "Vermont, Vital Records, 1760–1954" database corroborates this with an entry naming the same parents for the same event. Both are derivative and carry indeterminate-quality parentage information, but both are unambiguous in naming David Bagley.

**Pathway 2 — Sibling birth records.** David Bagley is named as the father of John Andrews Bagley (born 1807, Topsham) and Sophia Andrews Bagley (born 1812, Topsham) in two separately created birth registrations. These registrations are independent of one another and of the 1884 death record; each carries primary-quality information from a parent-informant present at the time of registration. Together they establish that David Bagley was fathering children bearing the Bagley surname in Topsham throughout 1807–1812, directly preceding William's birth circa 1815. The shared middle name "Andrews" in both John *Andrews* Bagley and Sophia *Andrews* Bagley strongly implies a mother whose surname or family name was Andrews—consistent with the death record's notation of "Sarah A. Bagley" as William's mother, reinforcing that all three children belonged to the same family unit.

No source of any type—vital record, census, indexed probate, land record, or memorial record—names any other person as William A. Bagley's father. No competing "David Bagley" in Topsham is suggested by any searched record.

### Conflicts

No conflicting evidence was identified. A minor discrepancy between the birth year circa 1815 (from the vital records index) and approximately 1816 (back-calculated from William's stated age in the 1850 federal census) is readily explained by the well-documented imprecision of stated ages in antebellum census records and does not affect the parentage conclusion.

### Research Scope and Tier

Research was declared exhaustive on 24 September 2026, following searches across FamilySearch Vermont vital records (collections 1987653, 1784223, 2075288, 1675544, 1675549, 1675550), federal censuses 1820–1880, the indexed Vermont statewide probate collection (negative), the indexed Vermont land records collection (negative), Vermont marriage records, and Find a Grave. No birth record for William A. Bagley was located; this absence is consistent with the incomplete state of Vermont town vital registration for the period around 1815.

The conclusion is rendered at **probable** rather than proved because all four sources bearing on the parentage question are derivative (FamilySearch index entries; original Vermont town clerk registers were not directly examined), and the informant for the 1884 death record's parentage entries is unknown, leaving that information at indeterminate quality. The ceiling is partly structural—Vermont death records of this era did not customarily identify the informant, making primary-quality parentage information unattainable from that source—but a gap also exists: the browse-only Bradford and Randolph District Orange County probate volumes (approximately 75,694 images) were not browsed, and external repositories including the Vermont Historical Society and American Ancestors were not searched. A probate file or will for David Bagley that names his heirs would constitute direct evidence and would be the most productive next step for a researcher seeking to elevate this conclusion to proved.

### Conclusion

David Bagley was very probably the father of William A. Bagley of Topsham, Orange County, Vermont. The 1884 Vermont Town Clerk death record directly names David Bagley in the father field of William's death entry. Two independently created Vermont birth registrations—for John Andrews Bagley (1807) and Sophia Andrews Bagley (1812)—corroborate that David Bagley was fathering children in Topsham throughout the decade before William's birth, with the shared "Andrews" middle-name pattern consistent with the same family unit named in the death record. No source of any type suggests an alternative candidate.
